# Defensive-code and over-engineering signatures — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Defensive-code and over-engineering signatures. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-09-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Practitioner signature list of AI-grown bloat: verbose scaffolding layers, partial fixes, ceremonial state layers mirroring other layers, non-functional placeholder subsystems left wired in, debug harness code in shipping source, and defensive abstractions that accumulate each agent turn; one Flutter app shrank 31.7% with tests passing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-01) — https://dev.to/maximsaplin/debloating-the-ai-grown-codebase-2om

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Across four LLMs, generated code had on average 63.34% more code smells than reference solutions (73.35% implementation smells, 21.42% design smells), with larger increases on more complex tasks. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03029

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Search-result snippets (not fetched) report opposite security-study findings: LLM code lacking defensive constructs, and one model with error handling in only 3.3% of scripts. Excess defensiveness is not established as a general LLM tell. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19182

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] GitClear's analysis of 211M changed lines (2020-2024) reports copy/pasted lines rising from 8.3% to 12.3% of changed lines while moved (refactored) lines fell from 25% to under 10%, read as assistants adding new code rather than reusing existing functions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-01) — https://www.gitclear.com/ai_assistant_code_quality_2025_research

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Agent-generated code shows procedural bloat (Long Method dominant) on simple tasks and architectural decay (God Class, superficial file separation) in complex systems; total lines of code correlates with architectural degradation at rho=0.94. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2605.02741v1 · keywords: Defensive-code and over-engineering signatures · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03029
- [statement] More capable models can produce messier code as they try to handle every edge case, yielding excessively long methods; detailed prompts and few-shot examples did not reduce defects in that study. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2605.02741v1
